Surrogate Data Technique¶

The surrogate data technique has been developed to investigate the phase coherency of waves/structures observed.

reference:
https://royalsocietypublishing.org/rsta/article-abstract/366/1864/447/50838/Experimental-evidence-of-phase-coherence-of?redirectedFrom=fulltext
https://journals.aps.org/pre/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevE.75.046401
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1023/A:1025506124402

The key of this technique is to prepare two extreme datasets with fully-randomised and fully-correlated from the original dataset, and we compare the original data with the others and calculate the coherency of the original data.

We first decompose data into the frequency and phase ranges using Fourier transformations, and then only change the phase data to a randomized set and correlated set ($\phi=0$).
For each dataset, we now calculate the path length defined as, $$L(\tau)=\sum_t|x(t+\tau)-x(t)|,$$ where $\tau$ is the time lag. Finally, we calculate the following equation to obtain the phase coherency index $C_\phi$, $$C_\phi(\tau)=\frac{L_{PRS}(\tau)-L_{ORG}(\tau)}{L_{PRS}(\tau)-L_{PCS}(\tau)},$$ where ORG, PRS, and PCS are the original, randomised, and correlated data set, respectively.

nt=np.size(geb[strt:end,0])#np.size(geb['Epoch'][:])
dt=1/16    #[s]
t=dt*np.arange(nt)
lt=dt*nt
ww=sf.fftshift(sf.fftfreq(nt,dt))

### tapered function
wdw=0.5*(np.tanh((t-lt/20)/20)-np.tanh((t-19*lt/20)/20))#np.r_[np.zeros(nt//8),np.ones(6*nt//8),np.zeros(nt//8)]

plt.plot(wdw)
plt.title('tapered function')
plt.show()

dat=bz[strt:end]-bz[strt:end].mean()
dat=dat*wdw

### original data ###
forg=sf.fft(dat)
amp =np.abs(forg)
phi =np.angle(forg)
#####################

### phase randomized surrogate ###
#phir=phi+np.pi#np.random.permutation(phi)
#for it in range(100): 
#    phirr=phir+np.random.permutation(phir)
#phir=phir/100-np.pi
phir=np.random.permutation(phi)#np.pi*(1-2*np.random.rand(nt))
#phir=np.pi*(1-2*np.random.rand(nt))
phir[0]=0; phir[nt:nt//2:-1]=-phir[1:nt//2] #symmetric
fprs=amp*(np.cos(phir)+1j*np.sin(phir))
datr=np.real(sf.ifft(fprs))
##################################

### phase correlated surrogate ###
phic=np.zeros(nt)
fpcs=amp*(np.cos(phic)+1j*np.sin(phic))
datc=np.real(sf.ifft(fpcs))
##################################

### plot figure ###

def path_length(nt,dat):
    x=np.arange(nt)
    L=np.zeros(nt)
    for tau in range(nt):
        #jp=np.r_[np.arange(nt-tau)+tau, np.arange(tau)]
        #L[tau]=np.sum(np.abs(dat[jp]-dat[x]))
        L[tau]=np.sum(np.abs(np.roll(dat,tau)-dat[x]))
    return L

### calculate path length for each datasets
Lorg=path_length(nt,dat )
Lprs=path_length(nt,datr)
Lpcs=path_length(nt,datc)

### plot the path lengths
plt.figure(figsize=(8,4))
tt=dt*np.arange(nt)
plt.plot(tt,Lorg,label='original')
plt.plot(tt,Lprs,label='random')
plt.plot(tt,Lpcs,label='correlated')
plt.legend()
plt.xscale('log')
plt.yscale('log')
plt.ylabel('L')
plt.xlabel(r'$\tau \text{ [s]}$')
plt.show()

### caluclate and plot the phase coherence index 
Cphi=(Lprs-Lorg)/(Lprs-Lpcs)
plt.figure(figsize=(8,4))
plt.plot(tt,Cphi)
plt.xlabel(r'$\tau \text{ [s]}$')
plt.ylabel('$C_\phi$')
plt.xscale('log')
plt.ylim(0,1)
plt.show()
